exceptions.reason: CVE-2026-14257 is fixed by the backports pinned per release line in package.json overrides (1.1.18, 2.1.4, 5.0.9). Verified in the installed builds, not assumed: node_modules/**/brace-expansion/index.js on the 1.x and 2.x lines carries 'var EXPANSION_MAX_LENGTH = 4000000' with an explicit CVE-2026-14257 comment and applies it as the default options.maxLength. The advisory range is the flat '<=5.0.7', so scanners keep reporting the patched 1.x/2.x builds as vulnerable. Forcing 5.x everywhere remains impossible and this was re-verified on 2026-08-07: brace-expansion@5 exports an object ({ EXPANSION_MAX, EXPANSION_MAX_LENGTH, expand }) rather than a callable default, while minimatch@3 does 'var expand = require("brace-expansion")' then calls 'expand(pattern)' directly, so it would throw 'expand is not a function' at runtime. minimatch@3 and minimatch@9 are required by eslint, jest and electron-builder. 1.1.18 and 2.1.4 are the newest releases on their lines, so there is nothing further to upgrade to. Every affected instance is dev-only build/lint/test tooling; the production tree is clean and npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.
